question: Does the Li >= 5 periodic cluster theorem or D >= 3 minimum multiplicity follow from an already published Cartesian-product local-minimum-degree or diagonal-distance theorem?
assessment: No applicable stronger Cartesian-product theorem was located in this bounded primary-source challenge. This is not a proof of novelty. A directly relevant 2019 abstract remains unresolved and must be checked before any priority claim.

records.authors: German Luna, Samuel Reid, Bianca De Sanctis, Vlad Gheorghiu
records.title: A Combinatorial Approach to Quantum Error Correcting Codes
records.inspected: Section 2 Definition 2; Section 3 Theorem 1 and equation 5; Section 6 C5 example; text search Cartesian
records.source_claim: Diagonal distance minimizes union (symplectic) support in the binary kernel of [I|A]; joint X/Z at one vertex counts once.
records.comparison: For the nonisolated simple tori used here this agrees with min |S union Odd(S)|, so the JMM lead is genuinely about the relevant metric, not a separate count of X and Z operations.
records.limits: No Cartesian-product theorem occurs in this inspected preprint. It is the antecedent definition cited by the JMM abstract, not the missing 2019 result.

records.authors: Jerome Javelle, Mehdi Mhalla, Simon Perdrix
records.title: On the Minimum Degree up to Local Complementation: Bounds and Complexity
records.source_claim: Local minimum degree is min |S union Odd(S)| minus one. Main family lower bound concerns Paley graphs; a cited earlier result concerns hypercubes.
records.limits: No applicable Cartesian-product lower bound was located. Its cited hypercube antecedent was subsequently inspected in the author-uploaded full text and is recorded separately below.

records.title: The Diagonal distance of Codeword Stabilized Codes
records.inspected: Introduction Theorem A; Section II diagonal-distance definition; references; text search Cartesian
records.source_claim: For a graph without four-cycles, diagonal distance is either minimum degree or minimum degree plus one.
records.comparison: This does not apply directly to Cartesian products of two or more cycles, which contain four-cycles.
records.limits: A claim that absence of four-cycles always gives degree plus one would overstate this theorem. No Cartesian-product result was located.

records.authors: Peter Hoyer, Mehdi Mhalla, Simon Perdrix
records.title: Resources Required for Preparing Graph States
records.provenance: ResearchGate explicitly labels the displayed full text as author content uploaded by Mehdi Mhalla. HAL and Oxford PDF retrieval failed, but the author-uploaded article text was inspectable.
records.inspected: Appendix B, Lemma 17 and its proof, Proposition 18, Theorem 19; text search Cartesian
records.source_claim: Lemma 17 gives local minimum degree at least n/2 for the n-dimensional binary hypercube. Theorem 19 concerns generalized binary hypercubes joined at fixed Hamming distance.
records.comparison: The Lemma 17 cancellation-counting mechanism uses at most two common neighbors. On degree-2D tori that elementary argument yields only a lower bound D, not the desired 2D. No general Cartesian-product theorem in the inspected text makes the new threshold-five proof immediate.
records.limits: The statement is a lower bound for binary hypercubes, not an exact formula for products of arbitrary cycles. No claim is made that this exhausts all subsequent product literature.
